headline: This 2013 law temporarily suspended the federal debt limit and withheld congressional pay if Congress did not adopt a budget resolution by a set date.
what_it_does: It suspended the $16.394 trillion public debt limit through May 18, 2013. After that date, it replaced the old discretionary increase process with an automatic increase, but only for certain debt obligations issued or guaranteed by the federal government after enactment and needed to meet commitments due before May 19, 2013. It also required each house of Congress to place its members' pay in escrow if that house had not agreed to a budget resolution for fiscal year 2014 by April 15, 2013, with the pay released only after the house adopted a budget resolution or the 113th Congress ended.

who_it_affects.how: Their mandatory pay would be held in escrow after April 15, 2013, if their house had not adopted a fiscal year 2014 budget resolution, and released only once that resolution passed or the 113th Congress ended.
It could borrow under an automatic debt-limit increase starting May 19, 2013, but only for obligations tied to payments due before that date.

who_it_affects.group: Holders of federal government debt and guaranteed federal obligations
who_it_affects.how: The debt-limit change governs how much new federal borrowing could be counted during the suspension period and after May 18, 2013.

when_it_takes_effect: The debt limit suspension applied from enactment on February 4, 2013, through May 18, 2013; the automatic increase took effect May 19, 2013; the congressional pay escrow applied after April 15, 2013.
